title: Exact five-uniformity outside Koo--Kwon condition (42)
summary: Determine whether the complementary Koo--Kwon binomial parameters always have differential uniformity exactly five above the experimental threshold.

formal_statement.body: Let $q=p^n>4007$ with $p>3$ and $q\equiv3\pmod 4$, let $r=(q+1)/4$, and let $\chi$ be the quadratic character of $\mathbb F_q$. For $u\in\mathbb F_q^*\setminus\{\pm1,\,\pm(1-2^{r+1})/3\}$ satisfying $\chi(1+u)=(-1)^{r+1}\chi(1-u)$, define $F_{r,u}(x)=x^r(1+u\chi(x))$ and $\delta(F_{r,u})=\max_{a\in\mathbb F_q^*,\,b\in\mathbb F_q}|\{x\in\mathbb F_q:F_{r,u}(x+a)-F_{r,u}(x)=b\}|$. Must $\delta(F_{r,u})=5$ for every such $(q,u)$?

scope.domain: Differential uniformity of odd-characteristic finite-field binomials
assumptions: $r=(q+1)/4$ and $\chi$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb F_q$
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves $\delta(F_{r,u})\le5$ on the complement of condition (42) and verifies equality computationally for $4007<q<10000$. Exact equality remains unproved for every admissible field order $q>4007$ and every complementary parameter $u$.

citations.label: Koo--Kwon, complementary exact five-uniformity conjecture
citations.locator: Section IV, experimental paragraph after condition (42), p. 26

progress.summary: The source extrapolates exact five-uniformity to every admissible field order above 4007 and explicitly notes that a rigorous proof is missing.
